evidence: This asserts the text of the implementation under test (_processors.py), not its behavior; reformatting the same-behavior source (quote style, whitespace, splitting the literal) would fail it — Rule-4 refactoring-violation.
src/rebar/reducer/_processors.py:42: `_KNOWN_TICKET_STATUSES = frozenset(get_args(TicketStatus))` — test re-derives with the identical expression

The behavioral contract (raise on unknown status in snapshot) is at src/rebar/reducer/_processors.py:572-573 and is exercised only in test_plan_review_phase_reducer.py, not in this file that claims to guard the vocabulary.
advisory.finding: test_the_module_no_longer_lists_the_statuses greps the source text of the module under test (via inspect.getsource) as its assertion, rather than asserting behavior. It reads _processors.py source and checks the literal string '{"idea", "open", "in_progress"' is absent and 'frozenset(get_args(TicketStatus))' is present — a change-detector that breaks on behavior-preserving reformatting (single vs double quotes, whitespace, splitting the frozenset literal across lines) with no observable-behavior change.
merged_from: The new test file asserts the derived set equals frozenset(get_args(TicketStatus)) — the exact same expression used in the production line under test — rather than driving the observable behavior the change protects (process_snapshot raising ValueError on an unknown status). This convergence-twin oracle compares the derivation against itself and cannot distinguish a working snapshot-reader from a broken one; the file adds no test exercising the actual raise/accept behavior for the reducer's status vocabulary.
advisory.suggested_fix: Delete test_the_module_no_longer_lists_the_statuses; its intent (no stale literal copy) is already enforced behaviorally by the derivation-equality test plus the process_snapshot raise/accept tests in test_plan_review_phase_reducer.py.
